subject: ACES
title: Intro Sustainable Food Systems
degreeAttributes: Nat Sci & Tech - Life Sciences course.

restrictions: Restricted to students in the Agr, Consumer, & Env Sciences or Agr, Consumer, & Env Sci Admn department.
sections.sectionText: This course uses a guided, discovery-based learning approach designed for students to understand, apply, and analyze key principles of food and environmental systems: what food is, where it comes from, how it gets to our plate, what happens to food waste, and how it is interacts with the surrounding environment. Students will develop an understanding of the interrelatedness and interdependence of food and environmental system components. Students will also “experience the food system” through activities related to food production, processing, retail, and post-consumption operations. Students will gain foundational skills in systems-thinking and leadership. This course is for students majoring in Sustainability in Food and Environmental Systems or other majors with approval from the instructor.

sections.sectionText: This is a second 8-week course that includes a mandatory field trip to Panama over the winter break. There is a program fee, which includes round-trip airfare from Chicago, lodging, on the ground transportation costs, all program-related activities, and most meals. Scholarships are available. Please contact the ACES Study Abroad Office at aces-studyabroad@illinois.edu for more information. If the course is full and you would like to be added to the waitlist, please also email aces-studyabroad@illinois.edu.
